image_description: A close-up view of a silver alloy car wheel with five spokes. Through the gaps in the spokes, a disk brake assembly is visible, including a perforated metal rotor and a black caliper housing. The center cap features a logo (resembling Holden).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The circular shape of the rotor is clearly visible behind the wheel spokes. The perspective confirms it is a thin disc relative to its diameter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A dark, bulky component consistent with a brake caliper is visible clamping onto the outer edge of the rotor on the left side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wheel hub and lug bolts are completely occluded by the wheel's center cap and spokes; they cannot be seen.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface shows cross-drilled holes, which is a common feature of high-performance ventilated rotors. While internal fins aren't directly visible, the external features match the description of a performance rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Inside the caliper housing, the darker rectangular shape of the brake pad backing plate/friction material is discernible against the shiny rotor surface.
The hydraulic hose/line is typically located on the back or top of the caliper and is obscured by the wheel spoke and shadow in this angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct circular patterns of small holes (cross-drilling) are clearly visible on the face of the rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface appears uniformly metallic silver/grey. There is no obvious blueing or browning indicative of significant heat stress or wear.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper has a matte, textured finish consistent with cast metal components used in automotive applications.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The logo on the center cap resembles a real brand (Holden lion and stone) but the details are slightly melted and indistinct, lacking the sharp vector precision of a real photograph. It is recognizable but structurally soft.

The reflections on the silver alloy wheel are overly smooth and plastic-like. Real metal usually shows sharper, more complex micro-reflections. The edges where the spoke meets the background show slight blurring.
The connection between the caliper and the suspension/wheel hub area is vague and lacks clear mechanical definition, appearing somewhat fused into the shadows.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the image contains the specific mechanical components of a disk brake system and not just a generic wheel.
To verify the spatial relationship between the wheel spokes (foreground) and the brake rotor (background), ensuring no 'melting' or depth errors.
To check for clean boundaries between the caliper, rotor, and wheel spokes, detecting any fusion artifacts.
To assess the overall realism of materials (metal vs plastic look) and lighting consistency.

focus_areas: Boundary sharpness between wheel spokes and brake rotor
Mechanical plausibility of the caliper mounting
Texture realism of the metallic surfaces
Legibility and structure of the center cap logo
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact on the logo. Even if minor, AI often fails at rendering crisp brand logos. Also, evaluate if the lack of heat discoloration makes the brake look 'too new' or artificial, though this is not strictly an artifact. Check if the geometric depth auditor finds any issues with the spokes passing in front of the rotor.
